sections.title: Our pricing
sections.text: We don't offer fixed packages, because the price follows the scope of work. Here we explain the range we work within and the factors that decide where you fall in it.
sections.label: Our working range
sections.text_3: The final price is set after we review your site and agree on the scope of work. We don't commit to a number before that review.

sections.title: Six factors that decide where you fall in the range

items.heading: Site condition
items.text: A technically sound site gets started faster. A site that needs basic fixes uses up part of the effort before any optimization begins.

items.heading: Number of pages or products
items.text: Ten service pages and a catalog of thousands of products are very different to audit, implement and monitor.

items.heading: Market and competition
items.text: Competing for a commercial keyword in a crowded market takes longer work on content and authority.

items.heading: Scope of implementation
items.text: An audit and recommendations only, full implementation on your site, or implementation plus monthly follow-up.

items.heading: Content and development
items.text: Are writing and technical changes part of our scope, or will your team handle them?

items.heading: Platform
items.text: Customization limits differ between WordPress, Shopify, Salla, Zid and WooCommerce.

sections.title: What raises the cost and what lowers it
sections.heading: Raises the cost

items.label: A large catalog or a high page count.
A need for larger volumes of new content.
Accumulated technical issues that must be fixed first.
More than one market or language.

items_2.label: A technically sound, relatively modern site.
A defined scope that starts with fewer pages.
An in-house team that handles changes and content.
A platform that allows changes without custom development.
One clear goal instead of an open-ended scope.

sections.title: What you get free of charge
sections.text: Before any financial commitment, you get an initial review and a call that clarifies where things stand and what to prioritize. If the work isn't right for you right now, we'll tell you.

items.heading: Initial site review
items.label: A quick read of its condition and what's holding back its visibility.

items.heading: Free 30-minute call
items.label: We discuss your goal and the core problem.

items.heading: Written scope and price
items.label: A proposal that sets out what's included and what isn't.

sections.label: We agree on the scope and cost with you after the call.

sections.title: Review the scope of each group

items.question: Is the price monthly or a one-time fee?
items.answer: That depends on the type and scope of work. A build or audit project is priced differently from ongoing work, and we make this clear in the written proposal before we agree.

items.question: Why don't you offer fixed packages?
items.answer: Because a fixed package imposes a scope that may not suit your site. We define the scope after reviewing your situation, so the price is tied to the actual work.

items.question: What is the minimum budget to get started?
items.answer: Our published range starts at SAR 1,500, but the actual scope of work and what it includes are set after we review your site and your project's needs.

items.question: Does the price include content and development?
items.answer: It includes whatever we explicitly agree on. Content and technical changes can be part of our scope, or your team can handle them.

items.question: Does the price change over time?
items.answer: It changes when the scope changes, such as adding pages, markets or new services. We never change it without a written agreement.

items.question: How do I get a scope that fits my website?
items.answer: Send your website details through the consultation form. We review your situation, then set the right scope and price with you on the call.
